authority: This file is the single source of truth for authentication/security test requirements shared by CI and live staging testing.
maintenanceRules: Change a requirement here first; CI mappings and live pass/fail criteria must not be edited independently.
Any auth/security defect must map to an existing case or add a new LIVE-AUTH case, with CI regression coverage where technically possible and live coverage where deployment/provider behavior matters.
A live case with CI coverage=gap must state why repository CI cannot or does not yet cover it.
Invitation controls remain explicitly not-applicable until a real invitation feature is introduced.
Live automation must explicitly mark provider steps that require a human-operated consent flow; those steps are never reported as automated passes.
A live run reuses a disposable account/mailbox across compatible sequential cases and provisions another only when the next case requires a fresh identity or different role/state.

Staging Turnstile automation uses Cloudflare's official always-pass testing sitekey `1x00000000000000000000AA` and secret `1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA`, and still exercises server-side token verification; test keys must never be used in production.

For sequential account journeys, reuse the run's ordinary-member account and its mailbox; create another account only for a required clean initial state or a distinct privilege level. Reuse one privileged account for all cases it is authorized to cover.

steps: Reuse the run's disposable mailbox/account when it is in a clean state; create a mailbox and account only if the run does not already have one suitable for this signup journey.
Complete signup with valid required fields and a valid password.

pass: Exactly one account is created for the normalized email identity.

fail: Signup creates duplicate identities, skips required verification, leaks sensitive data, or lands in an unauthorized state.

evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Session fixation, token tampering, stale-session replay, and revoked-session reuse fail closed

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.

steps: Capture pre-login and post-login session state.
Verify session rotation/authority transition.
Attempt safe replay of stale/revoked/tampered session material only on disposable accounts.

For protected page routing, explicitly verify /dashboard, /admin, and /onboarding (plus representative descendants where applicable) redirect an unauthenticated or server-invalid session to /sign-in; separately verify a genuinely authenticated non-admin user still receives the configured authorization-denial behavior for /admin.

With an authenticated protected dashboard already open, invalidate that session server-side, then return focus to the browser without clicking a dashboard control or refreshing; verify the stale protected page immediately leaves for /sign-in.
pass: Authentication does not preserve attacker-controlled pre-auth authority; stale/revoked/tampered sessions are rejected by protected resources with a clean redirect/denial (307 to /sign-in for unauthenticated /dashboard, /admin, and /onboarding page access; null/401/403 for an API). An already-open protected page whose session later becomes invalid automatically leaves for /sign-in when the browser resumes/focuses and identity revalidation returns null, without requiring a click or manual refresh. An authenticated but non-admin account may still receive the deliberate branded 404 for /admin. An uncaught server error or a 404 caused solely by an expired/missing session is a failure.
fail: A stale, revoked, or tampered session grants authenticated authority, OR its rejection surfaces as an uncaught error/generic error boundary rather than a clean redirect/denial, OR an already-open protected page remains visible after session-loss revalidation (for example, only swapping to logged-out navigation until the user clicks or refreshes).

evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

ci.rationale: Cleanup of live external test identities/mailboxes is operational evidence, not a repository-only behavior.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
steps: For passing cases, remove disposable accounts/sessions/mailboxes according to the runbook.
For failed cases, preserve only the minimum state needed for debugging and record what was retained.
Ensure test admin roles and temporary privileged state are removed.
pass: No unnecessary disposable privileged state remains; failures retain enough bounded evidence for diagnosis; secrets are never stored in reports.
fail: Temporary privilege/test accounts are left uncontrolled or failure evidence contains secrets.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Invitation auth testing is explicitly not applicable to the current product model

ci.rationale: Current canonical auth evidence states there is no live invitation flow; privileged accounts are provisioned directly by Super Admin.

pass: No invitation flow exists in the deployed product model.
fail: A new invitation flow is introduced without first changing this case to applicable and adding CI/live coverage.
evidence: If an invitation feature is introduced, update this catalog in the same change before release.

cases.title: Ordinary member sessions use a 7-day idle timeout and 14-day absolute lifetime while privileged sessions retain strict limits

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use disposable ordinary-member and Administrator/Super Admin test identities.
steps: Authenticate as an ordinary member and verify the issued session remains valid beyond the former 30-minute idle and 12-hour absolute windows, using controlled test-time/session evidence rather than waiting in real time.
Verify the ordinary-member policy is 7 days idle and 14 days absolute, with activity refreshing only the idle timestamp and never the absolute deadline.
Authenticate as an Administrator or Super Admin and verify the privileged session still uses the existing 30-minute idle and 12-hour absolute policy.
Verify the Active sessions UI/listing applies the same role-specific idle policy and does not hide a still-valid ordinary-member session or retain an idle-expired privileged session.
pass: Ordinary-member sessions use a 7-day idle limit and fixed 14-day absolute limit; privileged sessions remain 30-minute idle and fixed 12-hour absolute.
Role-specific active-session listing matches token validity and activity never extends the absolute deadline.
fail: An ordinary member is still forced out by the old 30-minute/12-hour policy, a privileged account receives the longer member lifetime, or active-session listing disagrees with actual token validity.
cleanup: Sign out disposable sessions and remove any temporary privileged role/test state after evidence is captured.
evidence: Record role, issued/observed expiry policy, relevant session-list behavior, HTTP status, and any screenshot/trace needed to prove the deployed behavior. Never record cookie/token values.

cases.title: Signup, password reset and password change reject passwords found in known data breaches

ci.rationale: The range-check unit test stubs a matching HIBP suffix for deterministic coverage; the password-reset integration test covers the authorized reset boundary. The browser specs drive the real signup, reset and Security-page password-change forms against a local breach-API stand-in, including the operations alert and the documented fail-open behavior.

preconditions: Use staging.idoc.club, never redesign.idoc.club, a Vercel preview, or localhost.
Use only a disposable test account and mailbox. Staging shares the production database, so cleanup is required.

Use the designated test password `Password#1` (10 characters; meets the composition rules) for the live HIBP check. Confirm the range response reports a match before submitting it in signup or password reset; use only the disposable test identity.
steps: Use the run's existing disposable mailbox/account if it has not completed signup; otherwise create a clean identity only for this signup rejection case.
Enter the composition-compliant breached password at password creation and submit.
Verify the password is rejected with the breached-password message and no account is created.
For reset, use an existing disposable account, request password reset, and complete the required email OTP or privileged TOTP verification.
Enter the same currently confirmed breached password and submit.
Verify the password is rejected and the prior credential remains valid; then complete reset with a unique, non-breached password.

For self-service change, sign in as a disposable paid-up member, open Security settings, enter the current password and the same confirmed breached password as the new one, and submit; verify it is rejected and the current password still works.
pass: Both signup and password reset reject the breached password and allow retry with a unique password.
The rejected signup creates no account; the rejected reset does not change the existing password.
Neither the raw password nor its full hash is sent to HIBP; only the 5-character SHA-1 prefix is sent.

Self-service password change also rejects the breached password and leaves the current credential unchanged; any configured operations alert names the flow and account and never contains the password.
fail: Either flow accepts the breached password, changes account state before rejecting it, or sends the raw password/full hash to HIBP.
cleanup: Complete a successful reset for the disposable account, then remove disposable account state after evidence is captured.
evidence: Record the test flow, whether HIBP reported the selected password as pwned, visible validation result, and account-state outcome. Never record the password, its hash, OTP/TOTP, cookies, or tokens.

cases.title: Member archive and permanent deletion enforce authorization, billing guards, and audit retention

ci.rationale: The disposable PostgreSQL integration test invokes the same transaction helpers used by the member actions and verifies permanent purge, archive retention, active-subscription and active-role guards, audit actor redaction, immutable-history trigger authorization, and atomic rollback. Shared tests cover the Server Action MFA and CSRF boundaries.

preconditions: Use the designated staging hostname and a disposable ordinary-member identity.
Use an identity with no active Stripe subscription; never select an administrator, Super Admin, or the acting administrator.
Capture the member-linked audit events before the test.
steps: As an administrator with fresh MFA, archive the disposable member and confirm sign-in is denied while profile, payment, registration, and audit records remain.
For a second disposable member with no active subscription, permanently delete the member.
Attempt the same operations with an active subscription and verify both are rejected before any records change.
Verify the deletion preserves audit events with actor_id cleared and removes the member account and linked records.
pass: Archive removes sign-in and revokes sessions while retaining related records.
Permanent delete removes the member account and configured linked records, retains audit event rows with null actor references, and is atomic.
Active subscriptions and privileged/self identities are never changed.
fail: An unauthorized/CSRF-forged or non-step-up action succeeds; a protected identity is changed; active billing is left chargeable; audit rows are deleted or changed beyond actor redaction; or a failed delete partially purges data.
cleanup: Keep evidence of audit-row preservation and the active-subscription guard; remove disposable state only after evidence is captured.
evidence: Record URL, administrator role, action, response, relevant audit-row IDs and before/after table counts. Do not record credentials or payment secrets.

cases.title: Paid member journey: membership entitlement and seminar payment are granted only by verified provider events, and seminar registration rules hold

ci.rationale: The browser specs run the real app and Stripe SDK against a local Stripe stand-in with webhooks signed by Stripe's own SDK; the Stripe-hosted payment page remains covered by the opt-in tests/stripe-e2e suite.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.

The staged deployment must be using Stripe test-mode credentials and have a published, fee-bearing test seminar; never use live-mode keys. Staging shares the production database, so cleanup is required.
steps: Reuse the run's ordinary-member account if it is still in a clean unpaid state; otherwise create one fresh member and reuse it for the paid membership and seminar steps.
Start membership checkout and return from Stripe without paying; confirm entitlement is not granted by the return redirect alone.
Pay with a Stripe test card and wait for the verified webhook; confirm entitlement becomes active exactly once.
Register for a seminar by each enabled payment method; for online payment complete Stripe test checkout and confirm the registration becomes paid once.
Confirm a full seminar and a seminar past its registration deadline reject registration with a clear message, and that cancellation updates My Seminars.

Confirm My Seminars/Courses shows both Payment Status and Registration Status (Confirmed for a non-FEI seminar, Pending FEI Approval for an FEI one), and that in a signed-out browser the seminar detail page offers no Register button or guest path.
pass: Entitlement and seminar payment status change only after a verified provider event, never from browser redirects or client-supplied fields.
Redelivered events do not double-credit.
Capacity, deadline, disabled payment methods and unpaid-member restrictions are enforced server-side.
Seminar/course registration is members-only: a signed-out or non-entitled visitor can browse details but cannot register by any route, and no guest or non-member pricing path exists.
fail: Entitlement or paid status is granted without a verified event, is granted twice, or a closed/full/disabled option accepts a registration.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: A canceled membership works through its paid-through date and then ends the relationship: the session ends and sign-in is refused

ci.rationale: The browser spec drives self-service cancellation through the real UI and moves the paid-through date to prove both sides of the boundary; sign-in refusal is exercised through the real password form. Integration regressions also prove that cancellation stops a pending renewal Subscription Schedule with no subscription row, retains failed schedule evidence for retry, and ends an activated schedule subscription at period end. A regression simulates activation between schedule retrieval and release.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
Use a disposable, paid-up member. Staging shares the production database, so cleanup is required.
Moving the paid-through date requires administrator entitlement correction; record the original value first.
Stripe test mode only: staging must use the test-mode keys and the communications and billing hold; never a live card.
steps: Sign in as the paid-up disposable member and cancel the membership from My Membership, confirming the dialog.
Confirm the member stays signed in with full access and My Membership shows when access ends.
Have an administrator move the paid-through date to yesterday (entitlement correction, with a reason).
Reload any page in the member's session and confirm it is signed out, then attempt password sign-in.
Have an administrator reverse the cancellation and confirm sign-in works again.

Before the cancellation, open Pay on My Membership and leave the Stripe Checkout page unpaid. After the administrator cancels (or suspends) the membership, complete that Checkout Session with a Stripe test card.
Confirm the membership status and paid-through date are unchanged, the payment is recorded, and a status_conflict reconciliation finding names the Checkout Session.
With the membership suspended (or review required), confirm Pay refuses to create a new Checkout Session.

Using only a disposable Stripe test-mode member, authorize a future automatic-renewal schedule, cancel membership, and confirm the schedule is released and cannot activate. Repeat through the administrator cancellation action.
pass: Cancellation never removes access before the paid-through date and any Stripe subscription is set to end at period end.
After the paid-through date the existing session ends and password sign-in is refused, with the canceled-membership message shown only after a correct password.
An administrator's reversal restores sign-in.

Completing a Checkout Session never reactivates or extends a canceled, suspended or review-held membership (pentest finding 5): the payment is recorded, entitlement is unchanged, a reconciliation finding is raised, and only the audited administrator reinstatement restores access.
Cancellation stops pending automatic-renewal schedules even when no subscription exists; failed provider cancellation remains visible and retryable.
fail: Access ends before the paid-through date, continues after it, or the refusal message is shown for an incorrect password or an unknown email.
A payment reactivates a canceled, suspended or review-held membership, or extends its paid-through date, without an administrator's audited action.
A pending renewal schedule can charge after membership cancellation, or a failed provider attempt clears the schedule evidence.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: An expired protected-page session returns the user to the same page after sign-in, and active use keeps an administrator signed in

ci.rationale: Unit tests cover the return-to path allow-list (protected same-origin paths only, no absolute or protocol-relative URLs) and the keep-alive wiring; the end-to-end return needs a real expired session and is exercised live.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
Staging keeps DISABLE_MEMBER_COMMUNICATIONS_AND_BILLING=true; only authentication OTP to this run's disposable @pixelsmith.space mailbox may be delivered.
Use a disposable member account; an administrator account is optional for the idle-limit check.
steps: Sign in and open a deep protected page such as /dashboard/profile?tab=security.
Sign out in another tab (or let the session expire), then reload the first tab and confirm it lands on /sign-in.
Complete sign-in (password, email code and MFA as required) and confirm the browser returns to the original deep page.
Request /sign-in?next=https://example.com and a signed-out visit to /api/user, sign in, and confirm neither is used as a destination.
As an administrator, keep clicking and typing on a protected page for longer than the 30-minute idle limit and confirm the session stays valid.
pass: Sign-in returns to the originally requested protected page exactly once; the remembered destination is cleared afterward and never points outside /dashboard, /admin, or /onboarding.
An actively used privileged session is not signed out by the idle limit, while an untouched one still expires.
fail: Sign-in lands on a different page after a protected-page redirect, honors an off-site or non-protected destination, reuses a stale destination on a later sign-in, or signs out an actively used session.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Imported WordPress passwords failing the current policy require a verified reset; compliant ones upgrade seamlessly

ci.rationale: Credential-format and policy checks run in CI, including the contract that a successful activation-link submit redirects to /sign-in with a flash notice instead of leaving the form on screen; the disposable WordPress fixture, real activation email and first-login browser lifecycle run against staging.

preconditions: Run against staging.idoc.club with DISABLE_MEMBER_COMMUNICATIONS_AND_BILLING=true and the staging-only authentication email exception enabled.

Provision two new disposable @pixelsmith.space mailboxes, and atomically seed corresponding migrated_pending members, current membership entitlements, professional-role/profile records and migration mappings only in idoc_staging.
Use a supported, verifiable WordPress bcrypt hash for each: one policy-noncompliant and one policy-compliant password. Never reuse real member accounts.
steps: Successfully enter the noncompliant imported WordPress password. Verify the explicit IDOC password-policy explanation and absence of a valid session.
Receive a real activation link at the disposable mailbox, open it, set a compliant password, and verify successful activation.
Try the original noncompliant password again and verify it is rejected.
Successfully enter the compliant imported WordPress password and verify the ordinary email OTP, first-login activation, and profile/onboarding destination without a mandatory reset.
Use a separate disposable breached-password fixture in a follow-up acceptance run to confirm the breach-specific explanation takes precedence if both checks fail.
pass: Policy-noncompliant verified WordPress credentials never establish a session without replacing their password through the received, single-use email link.
The old credential fails after replacement and a compliant imported WordPress credential proceeds without mandatory reset.
fail: Noncompliant imported password creates a session, its required-reset explanation is missing, no activation email arrives, the old password remains accepted after reset, or a compliant legacy credential is unnecessarily forced to reset.
cleanup: Neutralize only the disposable staging accounts through the authorized e2e cleanup helper; delete both disposable mailboxes.
evidence: Capture browser assertion results, delivery of the activation link, the staging revision, OTP and final destination. Never log or retain raw hashes, passwords, activation tokens or mailbox credentials.

cases.title: A pre-issued email-verification link cannot undo a suspension or deletion, rebind the login email afterward, or promote a legacy account

ci.rationale: Real-Postgres integration tests suspend, delete and migrated_pending-mark an account holding a captured verification token and prove redemption is refused, the link is burned and the account is untouched; suspension, self-deletion and bulk archive retire outstanding links.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
Use a disposable member with a password and a second disposable mailbox for the new address.
An administrator is needed to suspend and reinstate the disposable member.
steps: As the disposable member, request a login email change to the second mailbox (with the current password) and capture the verification link from that mailbox without opening it.
As an administrator, suspend the member.
Open the captured link and confirm the page reports the link unavailable.
Confirm the member is still suspended, the login email is unchanged, and the old address still cannot sign in.
Reinstate the member and confirm the link is still dead (it was burned or retired by the suspension).
Open /verify-email with an invalid token and confirm no session cookie is issued by the page.
pass: A verification link issued before an administrative suspension or self-service deletion is refused and burned; the suspension holds, the login identity does not move, and /verify-email never starts a session (pentest finding 4).
fail: Opening the pre-issued link lifts the suspension, restores a deleted account, rebinds the login email, or sets a session cookie.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Anonymous endpoints that cause email cannot be driven by unauthenticated callers beyond shared limits, and cannot carry caller-chosen text to staff

ci.rationale: Unit tests prove the alert path takes only a same-host plain path and a character-restricted browser string, that the route applies the shared database limiter per caller and deployment-wide, and that the unauthenticated resendVerification action no longer exists; the cross-instance volume behaviour needs the deployed platform.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
The Technical Support recipient mailbox must be a disposable @pixelsmith.space address for the run so alert content can be inspected.
steps: POST to /api/client-error repeatedly (at least 15 times within a few minutes, including from concurrent connections) with a hostile Referer such as a sentence containing a URL and a hostile User-Agent.
Confirm every response is HTTP 200 with a correlation requestId (the caller is never blocked from its reference).

Inspect the Technical Support mailbox: confirm the number of alerts stays within the shared limit (per caller address and deployment-wide) rather than scaling with concurrency, and that no alert subject or body contains the hostile Referer or User-Agent text.
Confirm there is no anonymous way to trigger an email-verification email (the old resendVerification action is gone): signup, login and recovery sends remain bound to their rate-limited OTP flows.
pass: Alert volume from anonymous client-error reports is bounded by the shared database limiter, the page named in an alert is a same-site path or absent, and no caller-chosen text reaches the alert subject or body (pentest findings 2 and 3).
fail: Alert volume scales with concurrent requests, an alert carries caller-chosen Referer or User-Agent text, or an unauthenticated caller can trigger a verification email.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Rich-text content cannot inject live markup into public pages or transactional emails

ci.rationale: Unit tests prove stray, unterminated, underscore-named, comment and processing-instruction markup is escaped by both sanitizers, that sanitizing twice is stable, and that ordinary editor HTML is unchanged; rendering in a real browser and the deployed CSP are verified live.

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
An administrator saves a disposable, unpublished article; delete it afterward.
steps: As an administrator, save an unpublished article whose HTML contains an unterminated image tag with an event handler, an underscore-named tag (<img_x onerror=...>), a comment opener and a meta refresh.
Publish it to a staging-only slug, open the public page as an anonymous visitor, and inspect the DOM.
Confirm the payloads appear as visible text, no img/meta/div_x element with those attributes exists, and the browser is not redirected.
Confirm ordinary formatting (headings, bold, lists, links, an image) in the same article still renders normally.
pass: Unrecognised markup is shown as text and never becomes an element, while normal WYSIWYG formatting is preserved (pentest finding 6).
fail: Any injected element, handler attribute or redirect appears in the rendered page or an email body, or normal formatting is lost.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
Delete the disposable article.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Member password changes and session revocation require fresh purpose-bound single-use email proof

ci.rationale: Regression checks cover both protected actions, separate OTP purposes, the consumed-code verification boundary and the in-place browser challenge. Real mailbox delivery and concurrent replay require deployed verification.

automation.reason: Requires possession of a disposable member mailbox and deliberate session/password revocation.

preconditions: Use a disposable entitled member account and mailbox on staging, never a real member credential.
Create two signed-in devices; keep a second copy of the active session before testing.
steps: Change the member password using the known current password; confirm a separate emailed security code is required before mutation.
Try a wrong or expired code; confirm the password does not change. Enter the correct code; confirm the change completes and sessions are revoked.
Sign in on two devices; revoke one session and then all other sessions; verify each action requires a new emailed security code and without it no session is revoked.
Try to use a password-change code to approve session revocation, reuse a consumed code, or replay it from another browser; each must fail.
For an administrator, confirm the existing authenticator TOTP challenge remains the required factor.
pass: Member password and session security mutations occur only after consuming a correct, user-bound, purpose-bound code, and privileged accounts continue requiring TOTP.
fail: Any mutation proceeds with only an existing session or with an invalid/replayed/cross-purpose code, or administrator TOTP is bypassed.
cleanup: Remove disposable devices and accounts once evidence has been recorded.
evidence: Record role, intended operation, time, result and masked email delivery evidence. Never record passwords or OTPs.
